runs.text: 1. Why does a computer understand binary values?
Computer memory is designed to store binary states represented as:
These binary values are the basic form in which information is represented inside computer memory.
2. How many bits make one byte?
A bit is a basic unit of computer memory capable of representing one of two binary values:
4. What electronic component is associated with storing a bit?
is described as the electronic component capable of holding one of two states corresponding to binary
5. What happens to RAM when the operating system starts?
The operating system assigns addresses to memory locations in RAM so that different locations can be identified and accessed.
Data can be stored in memory, but later the program must be able to locate and retrieve that data.
Memory addresses provide a way of identifying where data is stored.
7. Why is storing data alone not sufficient in programming?
Stored data is useful only if it can be retrieved when required.
Retrieving stored data is necessary for calculations, printing, comparisons, and other operations.
name given to a memory location in order to store and retrieve data
9. Why are variables used instead of directly remembering memory addresses?
Remembering numeric memory addresses is difficult.
Variables provide meaningful names for memory locations, making stored data easier to access.
easier to work with than raw memory addresses.
10. How should variable names generally be chosen?
A variable name should preferably indicate the type of information stored in it.
Meaningful names make the purpose of stored data easier to understand.
11. What kinds of real-world data may need to be stored in a computer program?
In Java, String values are enclosed within double quotes.
13. How is a character value written in Java?
A character is enclosed within single quotes.
A String, on the other hand, uses double quotes:
14. What kind of values does a Boolean represent?
A Boolean represents two logical values:
15. How can the value stored in a variable be accessed?
The variable name refers to the memory location containing the value.
It provides one environment containing the tools needed for activities such as:
Without an IDE, different environments may be needed for different activities.
An IDE integrates these activities into a single environment.
A syntax error occurs when code violates the grammatical rules of the programming language.
If the required semicolon is missing, compilation fails because the statement is syntactically incomplete.
Declaration means specifying a variable and its type.
Initialization means assigning a value to a variable for the first time.
was already declared, this gives it its first value.
Declaration and initialization together are referred to as defining a variable.
Reassignment means giving a new value to a variable that already contains a value.
Type inference is the process of determining the data type of a variable using the value assigned to it.

variable be initialized when it is declared?
With type inference, the variable's type is determined from its assigned value.
provides enough information to determine the type.
